thread:
maria: Heads up — while bringing up the new quantized zeta-7 variant in the eval harness I found raw prompt fragments leaking into the runner logs and saved artifacts. Repro on my laptop with --quantize=8bit.
sasha: ugh. can you paste the exact log snippet? were redact hooks enabled? :thinking_face:
maria: here's the relevant tail of the runner log (sanitized only a bit):

```
INFO 2025-06-18 14:02:12 runner.py:241 handling request id=req_abc123
PROMPT: "Customer: my api key is sk-live-12345, also account 9876"
REDACTION: applied=partial patterns=token_rewriter
Saved artifact: s3://redwood-evals/tmp/req_abc123/full_prompt.txt
```
You can see the token-level redaction replaced only substrings after tokenization mismatch; full_prompt.txt still contains the raw prompt because we save pre-detokenization.
aj: that explains why the CI gate didn't catch it — our eval-ci redaction test asserts logs contain `REDACTION: applied`, not artifact contents. The artifact check was skipped because the harness writes to an ephemeral local dir and the CI mock doesn't mirror the upload path.
sasha: repro notes — quantized model pipeline chunks prompts differently (kv cache chunking) so our regex-based redactor runs before reassembly. quick hack: run redaction after final string assembly and before any write/upload. but that's racy with streaming.
chuck: propose small fix + tests: 1) make redact() idempotent and run as the last step in Runner._finalize_response(); 2) add unit test that serializes a prompt containing a synthetic secret and ensures it is never present in any saved artifact or emitted log; 3) add an integration test in CI that actually pulls the artifact from the test S3 bucket and validates absence. patch sketch:

```py
# runner/runner.py (draft)
def _finalize_response(self, ctx):
    assembled = ctx.assembled_prompt  # post detokenize/reassembly
    cleaned = redact(assembled)
    ctx.safe_artifact = cleaned
    upload_artifact(ctx.safe_artifact, path)
    logger.info(f"Saved artifact: {path} (redacted)")
```
kevin: security notes — if CI starts pulling artifacts from S3 there's an ACL risk. Please use a dedicated test bucket with block-public-access, server-side encryption, and restrict GetObject to the CI service principal only. Also enable S3 Object Lock retention for the test namespace so accidental leaks are easier to flip to read-only while we investigate.
maria: agree re: bucket policy. also thinking we need RBAC for eval artifact viewing in the console — currently "eng" role can list all eval artifacts. we should add a label `sensitive=true` when any run touches customer-like input and only show to `eval-owners` + `security`.
sasha: sounds good. on the metric side, I noticed a drop in perplexity on the quantized variant vs fp16 on the eval dashboard (per-run avg dropped 1.4 points) — could be tokenization mismatch or the same prompt assembly bug causing truncated context. adding a metric that checks token-count equality between saved artifact and original request might help detect this class of bug earlier.
aj: CI wiring: I'll add a post-run hook in the eval-runner GitHub action that, after the harness finishes, downloads artifacts from the test bucket and runs a small redaction smoke test. We can gate PRs to require the smoke test to pass for changes touching runner.* and harness.* files.
eval-ci-bot: deploy-checks: artifact-redaction-smoke-test queued on runner-pr-842, ETA ~3m
kevin: one more ops control: audit logs for artifact access should be forwarded to our audit-log-collector and retained for 90d. If anyone manually downloads an artifact flagged as sensitive, the system should create an alert in #incidents and ping @security.
maria: OK I'll open a follow-up PR for the redaction location fix + unit tests. aj — can you own the CI artifact pull? kevin — will you add the bucket policy snippet for the docs and the account-level audit hook?
aj: yep, will do. thanks for catching this — small bug, big exposure risk.
sasha: if anyone wants to repro locally ping me, I have a tiny script that reproduces the detokenization race: `scripts/repro_quant_redact.sh`

maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
